whatTheyArgued: Jean-François Champollion (1790–1832), the decipherer of Egyptian hieroglyphs, read in the standard account and in his own Lettre à M. Dacier (1822): a language whose grammar is entirely unreceived is entered not by guessing its words but by finding a STRUCTURE ALREADY KNOWN IN ANOTHER SCRIPT and walking the parallel — the Rosetta stone's trilingual decree, Greek already readable, gave the grid; the proper names (Ptolemy, Cleopatra) gave the fixed points; and once the phonetic system was pinned, the grammar's own internal logic (the demotic and hieratic by-forms) let him read what no parallel covered. Two laws visible in his method: (1) the parallel fixes the KNOWN, never the unknown — Greek on the stone was not 'Greek content' but the grid of positions; (2) a name is a rigid pin, deciphered not by meaning but by its own recurrence within the known grid. He was wrong about which names first; the method, not the guess, is the inheritance.

scholarship.ref: Champollion, Lettre à M. Dacier relative à l'alphabet des hiéroglyphes phonétiques (1822), standard reading as transmitted in the on-disk corpus
scholarship.supports: the Cartesian grid method: decipherment proceeds from a known parallel plus fixed proper-name points, then the grammar's own logic extends beyond the parallel
scholarship.disputes: the historical account attributes early successes partly to Young and to phonetic-vs-ideographic missteps that the method corrected; our use of the method does not depend on the disputed priority

ourUse: language-training.js: for every language that holds a POS prior (the native grammar: pos-deu, pos-ell, pos-eng, pos-san, pos-*, 65+ held) and a Rosetta parallel (the UN-UDHR in hundreds of languages; the parallel-classics), the trainer runs the seam, emits the EOT, and scores the four good-enough gates (THE-GOOD-ENOUGH-BAR): EO-native clauses, cast-is-beings-not-vocabulary, claims-survive-the-byte, genre-within-language. The Rosetta does NOT teach content to the reader in a language-specific way — it is the grid: the same 30 articles in every language align at the article boundary, so a language's own seams can be checked article-by-article against what the parallel says should be there.

bends.ours: the UDHR parallel provides content to verify (paragraph alignment, proposition presence).
bends.theirs: the Rosetta stone was a grid of POSITIONS and rigid proper-name pins, never content; Greek on the stone was not 'the meaning' but the coordinate system.
bends.ourNewForm: the Rosetta parallel is used ONLY as the coordinate grid (same boundary in every language), never as content the reader may copy procedurally.

bends.ours: proper names bind by recurrence and company within the known grid (the case-free cast; the seat before the verb).
bends.theirs: Ptolemy and Cleopatra pinned the phonetic system by their recurrence across the cartouche — names are fixed points, not dictionary lookups.
bends.ourNewForm: kept: a name is a pin found by position and recurrence, never by a wordlist — the same law English's case-free seat learned.
